title: Signature Refinement Journal
description: Signature edition: every refinement step is journaled — the law applied, the side conditions, the proof artifact — forming a complete derivation from spec to code. Anyone can replay the derivation and check each step; the program's correctness argument is a browsable artifact. This is a Signature original method.
method: Journal each step with (law, obligations, artifacts); replay verifies the chain; the derivation is the documentation.
usage: Journal automatically from the refinement tool; review derivations like code reviews.

demo.code:
print('derivation: spec -> [seq law] -> [loop law] -> code (14 steps)')
print('replay: all 14 steps verified -> CORRECT BY CONSTRUCTION')

title: Signature Morgan's refinement laws
description: Signature edition: Carroll Morgan's laws are the algebra of refinement: 30+ proved rules for introducing sequences, conditionals, loops, and assignments from specs. The laws compose — complex developments are just law applications in sequence, each checkable by tools like the Refinement Calculator.
method: Apply laws (e.g., sequential composition, loop introduction); discharge proof obligations; the derivation is the correctness argument.
usage: Learn the core laws (skip, assign, seq, alt, loop); derive the rest by combination.

demo.code:
print('law: x:[P, Q] ⊑ x:[P, R]; x:[R, Q] (sequential composition)')
print('applied with R = (0 <= x <= n) -> step proved')

title: Signature Action systems refinement
description: Signature edition: Action systems (Back) model reactive programs as guarded actions on shared state; refinement adds detail while preserving observable behavior. It's refinement calculus for concurrency — the rely/guarantee reasoning integrates with stepwise development of parallel programs.
method: Specify as actions with guards; refine by decomposing actions and adding variables; prove each refinement step.
usage: Model the reactive core as actions; refine toward the implementation architecture.

demo.code:
print('action: transfer when funds available')
print('refined: +logging, +retry; observable behavior preserved -> proved')

title: Signature B-Method industrial refinement
description: Signature edition: The B-Method took refinement to industry: Paris Metro Line 14 (driverless) and various railway signaling systems were developed in B, with 100,000+ proof obligations discharged. Abstract machines refine to implementations; Atelier B checks every step — refinement at a scale most methods never reach.
method: Write abstract machines; refine to concrete; prove with Atelier B; generate code from the final refinement.
usage: Use for safety-critical control; invest in proof automation for the obligation volume.

demo.code:
print('Metro L14: 86,000 proof obligations')
print('Atelier B: 99.2% automatic -> implementation proved, zero defects in service')

title: Signature Probabilistic refinement
description: Signature edition: McIver-Morgan extended refinement to probabilistic programs: specs include probabilistic choice, and refinement preserves not just correctness but probability distributions over outcomes. Randomized algorithms get the same stepwise development with quantitative guarantees.
method: Specify with probabilistic choice; refine preserving expectation properties; prove quantitative bounds at each step.
usage: Use for randomized algorithms where the quantitative bound is the requirement.

demo.code:
print('spec: P(success) >= 0.99')
print('refined implementation: P(success) = 0.995 >= 0.99 -> QUANTITATIVE REFINEMENT HOLDS')

title: Signature Refinement patterns catalog
description: Signature edition: Experienced refiners reuse patterns: 'introduce accumulator', 'strengthen invariant', 'split case analysis'. A catalog of named refinement patterns — each with its law applications and side conditions — turns refinement from art into engineering practice.
method: Match the development step to a catalog pattern; apply its law sequence; discharge its standard side conditions.
usage: Build the team's pattern catalog from completed developments; teach patterns, not just laws.

demo.code:
print('pattern: introduce accumulator')
print('laws: data refinement + loop introduction -> applied, side conditions proved')

title: Signature Event-B method
description: Signature edition: Event-B (Abrial) applies refinement to reactive systems: start with an abstract machine of events, refine through levels adding detail, proving each level refines the last. The Rodin platform discharges proof obligations; Paris Metro Line 14's safety software was developed this way.
method: Abstract machine -> refinement levels; prove guard strengthening and invariant preservation per level; Rodin manages obligations.
usage: Refine in small levels; keep each level's new detail minimal; let Rodin track obligations.

demo.code:
print('M0: abstract doors; M1: +sensors; M2: +timing')
print('Rodin: 214 obligations, 208 auto, 6 interactive -> all discharged')

title: Signature Loop introduction with variants
description: Signature edition: The loop-introduction law turns a spec into 'do G -> body od' given an invariant and a variant (termination measure). It's the refinement-calculus twin of the decreases clause: the loop is correct and terminating because the law's side conditions say so, proved at introduction time.
method: Provide invariant + variant; prove the body preserves the invariant and decreases the variant; apply the loop law.
usage: Design the invariant and variant before the loop body; the law does the rest.

demo.code:
print('invariant: 0<=i<=n; variant: n-i')
print('loop law applied -> loop correct and terminating BY CONSTRUCTION')

title: Signature Data refinement (representation change)
description: Signature edition: Data refinement swaps abstract data for concrete representation — a set spec becomes a sorted list implementation — via a coupling invariant linking them. Prove the coupling invariant is maintained and every abstract operation refines to concrete code; the representation change is invisible to clients.
method: Define the coupling invariant; refine each operation; prove the invariant is established and preserved.
usage: Write the coupling invariant explicitly; it's the heart of the data refinement.

demo.code:
print('abstract: set S; concrete: sorted list L')
print('coupling: set(L) = S and sorted(L)')
print('operations refined, invariant preserved -> clients unaffected')
